reason: The literal premise holds and the defect class stands, but the write-up's specific curl/scheme-wildcard instantiation ('Bash(curl https *)') is not well-supported: the spec's own worked family-merge example (gh pr view 123 / gh pr view 456 -> family 'gh pr view') generalizes by dropping a whole TRAILING token that differs across grants, never by truncating a single shell word (a URL is one token) down to a substring like a scheme prefix -- two curl grants to different URLs do not share any literal token and would not merge into one family under that mechanism, so the specific 'unrestricted outbound HTTP(S) to any host' framing is an unsupported leap. The underlying defect is real and at least as severe through a cleaner instance the write-up does not foreground: ssh/docker-exec-style programs where the trailing argument (the remote command) is the one that varies across sessions and the preceding token (host/container) repeats -- e.g. 'ssh prod-host whoami' + 'ssh prod-host uptime' merge by the stated mechanism (program + leading shared token, trailing distinguishing token dropped, exactly like the gh example) into family 'ssh prod-host', deriving 'Bash(ssh prod-host *)' -- an auto-mergeable, auto-votable rule (smine-apply's permissions-kind route, SKILL.md:31, appends it to permissions.allow verbatim on a single + vote or in always-mode with no explicit permissions exclusion) that grants arbitrary remote command execution on that host with no further review. No special-case/literal-argument/known-safe-allowlist guard exists anywhere in smine-permissions' step 2 (verified both ways below), so this class of over-broad derivation for subcommand-less programs is confirmed; effect destructive and exposure rare both stand (precondition is >=2 sessions granting the same leading-token command, per step 4's stated gate) -- cells unchanged, no override needed, see reason for the corrected example.
